title: Hotel: overlapping reservations
summary: Two guests book the same room for overlapping nights through two booking channels.
background: A hotel sells rooms on its own site and through travel agencies. A reservation holds a room for a date range, stored as a daterange such as [2026-10-01, 2026-10-04). Two reservations for the same room must never overlap.

The naive service checks that no reservation overlaps the requested range and then inserts. A unique constraint cannot help because the ranges are different values that still overlap. Two channels checking at the same time both see a free room, both insert, and two guests arrive for the same bed.

Postgres has a constraint made for this: an exclusion constraint. EXCLUDE USING gist (room_id WITH =, stay WITH &&) rejects any row whose room is equal and whose range overlaps an existing row, and it is enforced across concurrent transactions the same way a unique index is. The btree_gist extension lets the gist index handle the plain integer room_id.

Adding the constraint to a live table fails while old conflicting rows exist: Postgres validates every existing row. The seed already holds one legacy double booking in room 102 (the self join exercise finds it), so the safe run first deletes the newer reservation of every overlapping pair and only then adds the constraint. In production that cleanup is a business decision, not a DELETE.

race.goal: Room 1 is empty for the next 10 nights. 20 channels try 2 random 2 night stays each. No two reservations of room 1 may overlap.
